notable_absence.finding: This worked example does not introduce anything beyond what the sibling page eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.json already registers: wildcard bucket-alias bindings scoped to 'bucket.scope.*', the meta.keyspace parameter, and the Advanced Keyspace Accessor operator family (couchbase.get/upsert/replace/delete/insert taking an explicit keyspace argument) are the exact same primitives used here. No new constraint or primitive specific to 'multi-collection' Eventing as such was found.

cross_component_finding: Answering the batch hypothesis directly: multi-collection Eventing does NOT introduce a new mechanism. It is the worked example of eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor + eventing:meta-keyspace-parameter (already reconciled from eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.json this round) applied via a wildcard 'bucket.scope.*' bucket-alias binding. The one operational nuance this page adds is a code comment showing *why* the mechanism is required: 'Protect against reading from something outside the alias' - a wildcard-scoped alias can otherwise be used to read/write any collection in that scope, so the handler must guard on meta.keyspace.scope_name/collection_name before acting.
